title: The Simulation Hypothesis
description: If reality is computed, it can be decompiled - and edited.

puzzle.goal: Any region that holds information must hold it in physical states, and a finite region with finite energy has finitely many. Write the maximum number of bits that fit in a sphere of radius R as 2πR/(ħc·ln 2) times its total energy, with that energy written as the volume integral (in spherical shells) of the mass density ρ(r) times c².
puzzle.name: Bekenstein bound (energy integrated over the region)
puzzle.ask: With the energy integral done, I = 2πRE/(ħc ln 2). Find the bound for a proton: R = @{R} fm, E = 938.3 MeV and ħc = 197.3 MeV fm.
puzzle.method: Entropy over kB is at most 2πRE/(ħc); bits are entropy divided by ln 2; a sphere's volume element is 4πr² dr.
